documentation.content:
One or more held symbols have had NO covered call written against them for >= the alert threshold (default 7 trading days), so that capital is idle.

Precedent: AMZN's 62-day gap (Feb-Apr 2026) cost an estimated $1,500-3,000 in foregone premium.

REPOINTED 2026-08-01 (FC-065 Phase 4). This alert used to report an 'FC-029 R3 drawdown pause' inferred from price vs the latest OPASN put strike. There is no drawdown gate any more (OQ-3), and since FC-065 Phase 1 the bot's floor is Alpaca's avg_entry_price - one put premium BELOW the strike that inference used - so near the threshold the alert and the bot disagreed. It now reads the bot's own options_wheel.decision_events records. The marker string, filter, channel and scheduler job are deliberately UNCHANGED: renaming the marker would silently disarm the alert.

Also matches DRAWDOWN_PAUSE_ALERT_CHECK_FAILED - the daily check could not evaluate, or could not derive uncovered_days for a held symbol. Treat that as 'unknown', not 'all clear'.

Triage:
1. Dashboard -> Bot Health -> Uncovered Positions.
2. Run the fill-rate query in docs/operations/DECISION_RECORDS.md. An EMPTY decision table means the bot is not writing records (rolled-back revision, BigQuery outage), not that everything is covered.
3. A symbol uncovered while ABOVE its floor means the delta/premium bands emptied the chain, not the floor - check reason_counts on its no_candidates row.

NOTE: the filter deliberately does NOT constrain severity. Cloud Run captures the app's stderr as plain text with EMPTY severity, so a severity>=WARNING clause matches nothing (verified by fire drill 2026-07-18). Payload shape is matched both ways so structured logging can be adopted later without breaking the alert.

Plan: docs/plans/fc-065.md. Runbook: deploy/monitoring/drawdown_pause_alert.md
